newsitem.title: USA: Petrolite to be acquired by Baker Hughes.
newsitem.headline: Petrolite to be acquired by Baker Hughes.

text.p: Petrolite Corp., a speciality chemicals maker, said Wednesday it has agreed to be acquired by Baker Hughes Inc. in a stock swap worth $61 per Petrolite share or about $693 million.
The deal includes Baker Hughes' acquisition of Wm. S. Barnickel & Co., a closely held company that is Petrolite's largest shareholder, it said.

Baker Hughes, a Houston-based company that sells oil and gas products and services, will offer $61 worth of its common stock for each of Petrolite's 11.36 million shares in a tax-free exchange. The exact exchange ratio will be based on the average market price of Baker Hughes stock over 10 days prior to closing, Petrolite said.
Petrolite's stock soared $10.25 to $58.25 on Nasdaq at mid-morning. Baker Hughes edged up 62.5 cents to $36.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The definitive agreement is subject to approval by shareholders of Petrolite and Barnickel, Petrolite said.
For its fiscal year ended Oct. 31, St. Louis-based Petrolite had sales of $361 million, down from $364.8 million a year ago.

Petrolite earlier this month put off its March 3 annual meeting, citing a possible sale or merger of the company. It said in November it had formed a special committee to explore sale or merger options and that it had rejected earlier offers of $44 per share or less as "clearly indaequate."
